thread:
incidents-bot: [ALERT] Elevated p99 latency and push-stream backlog in prod us-west-2 for push-response workers. Error spikes observed on push frames (SSE clients). Severity: P2 — possible customer degradation.

matt_oncall: oncall here, looking. which subset is it hitting? all customers or specific tiers?

priya_sre: metrics: push-frames backlog ~85k, worker cpu ok but gpus have KV cache thrash, p99 generation latency up ~3.2s (baseline 0.4s). errors are mostly 502/timeout from push-transport. A few downstream retries causing bursts.

matt_oncall: thanks. paging eng-sre for mitigation, paging support for comms. @tara_eng can you own immediate mitigation?

tara_eng: taking it. plan: temporarily disable server-initiated streaming (push frames) in us-west-2, shift clients to short-poll fallback, and tighten per-API-key rate limits to reduce burst. will coordinate with support.

tara_eng: executing feature flip now. command:

```
./ops/feature-toggle --env prod --region us-west-2 --flag push_streaming.enabled --value false --reason "mitigate push backlog, reduce p99"
```

jason_support: noted. drafting a short advisory for affected customers: "We’re temporarily switching streaming responses to polling in US-WEST-2 to stabilize latency. No data loss; responses may arrive via polling for ~30-60m." Will post to status page once you confirm.

tara_eng: flip complete. push_streaming.enabled=false in prod/us-west-2. immediate effect: backlog dropping, p99 down from 3.2s -> 0.48s within two minutes. error-rate down ~65%.

priya_sre: confirming telemetry: 5xx rate reduced from 1.9% to 0.6%, connection churn normalized. CPU/GPU utilization fell by ~18%. Good signal.

matt_oncall: thanks. I’m escalating to post-incident team to capture timeline. jason_support, please post the status message now. Include suggested customer remediation: increase client retry interval to 10s, fallback to polling endpoint: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/polling.

jason_support: posted on status.redwood.ai (incident 2026-1719502468). copy of notice: "We have temporarily disabled push streaming in US-West-2 to reduce latency and errors. Polling is available and recommended. Our engineers are working to re-enable streaming once safe."

tara_eng: follow-ups: 1) run deeper profiling on KV cache eviction patterns, 2) evaluate incremental rollout with rate-limited stream fanout, 3) prepare capacity bump for push workers if needed. I created a follow-up ticket: RDW-INC-4832.

priya_sre: also applied temporary rate limit adjustment to reduce noisy tenants:

```
./ops/quota-adjust --env prod --region us-west-2 --target nonpaid --rps 1 --note "emergency throttle"
```

matt_oncall: handoff: I will remain primary until follow-up ticket triaged. tara, priya — please sync on root-cause and timeline for safe re-enable. jason, please coordinate any customer requests.

tara_eng: agreed. target to re-evaluate in 30m with metrics. if stable, we’ll do a staged re-enable behind a strict rate shaper + canary.

priya_sre: metric checkpoint at +20m: p99 steady ~0.45s, backlog ~2k. continuing to watch.

matt_oncall: thanks team. closing alert channel for now; keeping incident ticket open for postmortem. :+1:

jason_support: drafted follow-up email for customers who opened tickets during the spike — will send once we have re-enable ETA.

tara_eng: leaving a short note in the incident ticket with commands we ran + diff of flags. will add recommended load tests before re-enable.

matt_oncall: ok official owner: tara_eng for mitigation actions, priya_sre for monitoring + root cause, jason_support for customer comms. re-eval in 30m.

(automatic) incidents-bot: Incident RDW-2026-1719502468 created and linked to RDW-INC-4832. Pager notifications suppressed for follow-ups.
